**Section 4.2.2 Dividends.** Subject to the preferential rights of the holders of Preferred Stock as set forth in this Certificate, the holders of shares of Common Stock shall be entitled to receive dividends and other distributions (payable in cash, property, or shares of the Corporation\'s capital stock) when, as, and if declared thereon by the Board of Directors from time to time out of any assets or funds of the Corporation legally available therefor. No dividends or other distributions shall be declared or paid on shares of Common Stock unless and until all dividends declared on the Preferred Stock (including all accrued but unpaid dividends, if any) have been paid in full or set aside for payment.

**Section 4.2.3 Liquidation.** Upon any Liquidation Event (as defined in Section 4.3.3 below), after the payment or provision for payment of all debts and liabilities of the Corporation, and after the payment of the full preferential amounts to which the holders of Preferred Stock are entitled pursuant to Section 4.3.3, the remaining assets of the Corporation available for distribution to its stockholders shall be distributed ratably among the holders of Common Stock on a per share basis. For the avoidance of doubt, the holders of Series A Preferred Stock shall participate in such distribution to the extent provided in, and subject to the terms and conditions of, Section 4.3.3 below.

**Section 4.3 Series A Preferred Stock.**

The rights, preferences, privileges, restrictions, and other matters relating to the Series A Preferred Stock are as follows:

**Section 4.3.1 Designation and Amount.** Six million (6,000,000) shares of the authorized Preferred Stock of the Corporation are hereby designated as \"Series A Preferred Stock.\" The Original Issue Price of the Series A Preferred Stock shall be Two Dollars (\$2.00) per share (the \"Original Issue Price\"), as adjusted for any stock splits, stock dividends, combinations, recapitalizations, or similar events with respect to the Series A Preferred Stock after the date hereof.

**Section 4.3.2 Dividends.** (a) The holders of the then-outstanding shares of Series A Preferred Stock shall be entitled to receive, when, as, and if declared by the Board of Directors, out of any assets or funds of the Corporation legally available therefor, non-cumulative dividends at the rate of eight percent (8%) of the Original Issue Price per share per annum (i.e., \$0.16 per share per annum, subject to appropriate adjustment in the event of any stock dividend, stock split, combination, or other similar recapitalization). Such dividends shall be payable in preference and priority to, and prior to the payment of, any dividends on shares of Common Stock. The right to receive dividends on shares of Series A Preferred Stock shall not be cumulative, and no right to such dividends shall accrue to holders of Series A Preferred Stock by reason of the fact that dividends on said shares are not declared or paid in any prior year.

\(b\) No dividends or other distributions (other than dividends or other distributions payable in shares of Common Stock) shall be paid on, or declared and set apart for, any shares of Common Stock during any fiscal year of the Corporation unless dividends have first been paid or declared and set apart for payment on the Series A Preferred Stock in an amount per share of Series A Preferred Stock equal to or greater than the aggregate amount of such dividends per share of Common Stock multiplied by the number of shares of Common Stock into which each share of Series A Preferred Stock is then convertible. In the event dividends are paid on any share of Common Stock, an additional dividend shall be paid with respect to all outstanding shares of Series A Preferred Stock in an amount equal per share (on an as-if-converted to Common Stock basis) to the amount paid or set aside for each share of Common Stock.

\(c\) The Board of Directors shall be under no obligation to declare dividends on the Series A Preferred Stock or the Common Stock in any fiscal year.

**Section 4.3.3 Liquidation Preference.** (a) **Liquidation Event**. For purposes of this Certificate, a \"Liquidation Event\" shall mean (i) any voluntary or involuntary liquidation, dissolution, or winding up of the affairs of the Corporation, or (ii) any Deemed Liquidation Event as defined in Section 4.3.4 below.

\(b\) **Preferential Payments to Holders of Series A Preferred Stock**. In the event of any Liquidation Event, before any payment or distribution shall be made to the holders of Common Stock or any other class or series of capital stock ranking junior to the Series A Preferred Stock, the holders of shares of Series A Preferred Stock then outstanding shall be entitled to be paid out of the assets of the Corporation available for distribution to its stockholders (whether such assets are capital, surplus, or earnings), an amount per share equal to the Original Issue Price for each outstanding share of Series A Preferred Stock, plus any dividends declared but unpaid thereon (the \"Series A Liquidation Preference Amount\"). If, upon the occurrence of a Liquidation Event, the assets and funds of the Corporation available for distribution to the stockholders shall be insufficient to pay the holders of shares of Series A Preferred Stock the full Series A Liquidation Preference Amount, the holders of shares of Series A Preferred Stock shall share ratably in any distribution of the assets and funds of the Corporation available for distribution in proportion to the respective Series A Liquidation Preference Amounts that would otherwise be payable upon such Liquidation Event with respect to the outstanding shares of Series A Preferred Stock held by each such holder if all such amounts payable on or with respect to such shares were paid in full.

\(c\) **Remaining Assets; Conversion Alternative**. After the payment of the full Series A Liquidation Preference Amount to the holders of Series A Preferred Stock pursuant to Section 4.3.3(b) above, the remaining assets of the Corporation available for distribution to its stockholders shall be distributed among the holders of shares of Common Stock, pro rata based on the number of shares of Common Stock held by each such holder. Notwithstanding the foregoing, in lieu of receiving the Series A Liquidation Preference Amount, each holder of Series A Preferred Stock may elect instead to receive the amount such holder would have received had all outstanding shares of Series A Preferred Stock been converted into Common Stock immediately prior to such Liquidation Event (without regard to any limitations on conversion set forth herein), based on the number of shares of Common Stock issuable upon such conversion and the aggregate amount available for distribution to all holders of Common Stock (including shares of Common Stock issued or issuable upon conversion of all shares of Series A Preferred Stock) on a pro rata per share basis. For the avoidance of doubt, each holder of Series A Preferred Stock shall be entitled to receive the greater of (i) the Series A Liquidation Preference Amount or (ii) the amount such holder would receive on an as-converted to Common Stock basis, but not both. This is a non-participating preferred stock structure.

\(d\) **Valuation of Non-Cash Consideration**. If any assets of the Corporation distributed to stockholders in connection with any Liquidation Event are other than cash, then the value of such assets shall be their fair market value as determined in good faith by the Board of Directors, except that any securities to be distributed to stockholders in a Liquidation Event shall be valued as follows:

> \(i\) If the securities are traded on a securities exchange, the value shall be deemed to be the average of the closing prices of the securities on such exchange over the thirty (30) trading day period ending three (3) trading days prior to the distribution;
>
> \(ii\) If the securities are actively traded over-the-counter, the value shall be deemed to be the average of the closing bid prices over the thirty (30) trading day period ending three (3) trading days prior to the distribution; and
>
> \(iii\) If there is no active public market for the securities, the value shall be the fair market value thereof, as determined in good faith by the Board of Directors of the Corporation.

**Section 4.3.4 Deemed Liquidation Events.** (a) **Definition**. Each of the following events shall be treated as a Liquidation Event for purposes of this Certificate (each, a \"Deemed Liquidation Event\"), unless the holders of at least a majority of the outstanding shares of Series A Preferred Stock (voting as a separate class) elect otherwise by written notice given to the Corporation at least five (5) days prior to the effective date of any such event:

> \(i\) A merger or consolidation of the Corporation with or into any other entity or entities (other than a merger or consolidation in which (A) the holders of capital stock of the Corporation immediately prior to such merger or consolidation continue to hold at least a majority of the voting power of the surviving or resulting entity (or its parent) immediately after such merger or consolidation, and (B) the shares of capital stock of the Corporation are converted into or exchanged for shares of capital stock of the surviving or resulting entity (or its parent) having substantially comparable rights, preferences, and privileges as the shares of capital stock of the Corporation held by such holders immediately prior to such merger or consolidation);
>
> \(ii\) A sale, lease, transfer, exclusive license, or other disposition, in a single transaction or a series of related transactions, by the Corporation or any subsidiary of the Corporation, of all or substantially all the assets of the Corporation and its subsidiaries taken as a whole, except where such sale, lease, transfer, exclusive license, or other disposition is to a wholly owned subsidiary of the Corporation; or
>
> \(iii\) Any transaction or series of related transactions (including, without limitation, any reorganization, merger, or consolidation, but excluding any transaction or series of transactions covered by clause (i) or (ii) above) in which in excess of fifty percent (50%) of the Corporation\'s voting power is transferred, other than the issuance of capital stock by the Corporation in a bona fide equity financing transaction the primary purpose of which is capital raising by the Corporation.

\(b\) **Treatment of Proceeds**. The funds and assets resulting from or arising out of a Deemed Liquidation Event shall be distributed in accordance with the provisions of Section 4.3.3 as though such Deemed Liquidation Event were a Liquidation Event, unless the holders of at least a majority of the outstanding shares of Series A Preferred Stock elect otherwise. The Corporation shall provide each holder of Series A Preferred Stock with not less than ten (10) days\' prior written notice of any Deemed Liquidation Event specifying in reasonable detail the material terms and conditions thereof.

\(c\) **Approval**. Any Deemed Liquidation Event shall require the prior approval of the holders of at least a majority of the outstanding shares of Preferred Stock, voting as a single class, in accordance with Section 4.3.8(v) hereof.

**Section 4.3.5 Conversion.** The holders of Series A Preferred Stock shall have the following conversion rights:

**(a) Optional Conversion.** Each share of Series A Preferred Stock shall be convertible, at the option of the holder thereof, at any time and from time to time, without the payment of additional consideration by the holder thereof, into such number of fully paid and nonassessable shares of Common Stock as is determined by dividing the Original Issue Price by the Conversion Price (as defined below) in effect at the time of conversion. The initial \"Conversion Price\" for the Series A Preferred Stock shall be the Original Issue Price (i.e., \$2.00 per share), as adjusted from time to time in accordance with this Section 4.3.5 (each such adjusted price, the \"Conversion Price\"). The initial conversion rate for the Series A Preferred Stock shall therefore be one-to-one (1:1), such that each share of Series A Preferred Stock is initially convertible into one (1) share of Common Stock, subject to adjustment as provided herein. In order to convert shares of Series A Preferred Stock into shares of Common Stock, a holder shall surrender the certificate or certificates therefor (or, if such holder alleges that any such certificate has been lost, stolen, or destroyed, a lost certificate affidavit and indemnity agreement reasonably acceptable to the Corporation), duly endorsed, at the principal office of the Corporation or any transfer agent for the Series A Preferred Stock, and shall give written notice to the Corporation of the election to convert the same, stating therein the number of shares of Series A Preferred Stock being converted. Such conversion shall be deemed to have been made at the close of business on the date of such surrender and receipt of notice, and the person or persons entitled to receive the shares of Common Stock issuable upon such conversion shall be treated for all purposes as the record holder or holders of such shares of Common Stock on such date.

**(b) Automatic Conversion.**

> \(i\) Each share of Series A Preferred Stock shall automatically be converted into shares of Common Stock at the then-effective Conversion Price, without any further action by the holder thereof, upon the earlier of (A) the closing of an underwritten public offering of shares of Common Stock of the Corporation pursuant to an effective registration statement under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the \"Securities Act\"), covering the offer and sale of shares of Common Stock to the public at a per share price of at least three times (3x) the Original Issue Price (i.e., at least \$6.00 per share, as adjusted for stock splits, stock dividends, recapitalizations, and the like), with aggregate gross proceeds to the Corporation of not less than Thirty Million Dollars (\$30,000,000), before deduction of underwriting discounts and commissions and expenses (a \"Qualified IPO\"), or (B) the date specified by the written consent or affirmative vote of the holders of at least a majority of the then-outstanding shares of Series A Preferred Stock, voting as a separate class.
>
> \(ii\) Upon the occurrence of either of the events specified in Section 4.3.5(b)(i) above, the outstanding shares of Series A Preferred Stock shall be converted automatically without any further action by the holders thereof and whether or not the certificates representing such shares are surrendered to the Corporation or its transfer agent; *provided, however*, that the Corporation shall not be obligated to issue certificates evidencing the shares of Common Stock issuable upon such conversion unless the certificates evidencing such shares of Series A Preferred Stock are either delivered to the Corporation or its transfer agent, or the holder notifies the Corporation or its transfer agent that such certificates have been lost, stolen, or destroyed and executes an agreement satisfactory to the Corporation to indemnify the Corporation from any loss incurred by it in connection therewith.

**(c) Anti-Dilution Adjustments.**

> \(i\) *Broad-Based Weighted Average Adjustment.* If the Corporation shall issue Additional Shares of Common Stock (as defined below) after the date of filing of this Certificate without consideration or for a consideration per share less than the applicable Conversion Price in effect immediately prior to such issue, then the Conversion Price for the Series A Preferred Stock shall be reduced, concurrently with such issue, to a price determined in accordance with the following formula:
>
> CP₂ = CP₁ × (A + B) / (A + C)
>
> where:
>
> \"CP₂\" means the Conversion Price in effect immediately after the issuance of such Additional Shares of Common Stock;
>
> \"CP₁\" means the Conversion Price in effect immediately prior to the issuance of such Additional Shares of Common Stock;
>
> \"A\" means the number of shares of Common Stock outstanding immediately prior to such issuance, calculated on a fully diluted basis (including all shares of Common Stock issuable upon conversion of all outstanding shares of Preferred Stock and upon exercise of all outstanding options, warrants, and other convertible securities, but excluding any Additional Shares of Common Stock being issued in such transaction);
>
> \"B\" means the number of shares of Common Stock that would have been issued if such Additional Shares of Common Stock had been issued at a price per share equal to CP₁ (i.e., the aggregate consideration received by the Corporation for such issuance divided by CP₁); and
>
> \"C\" means the number of Additional Shares of Common Stock actually issued in such transaction.
>
> \(ii\) *Definition of Additional Shares of Common Stock.* For purposes of this Section 4.3.5(c), \"Additional Shares of Common Stock\" shall mean all shares of Common Stock issued (or deemed issued pursuant to Section 4.3.5(c)(iii) below) by the Corporation after the date of filing of this Certificate, other than the following (collectively, \"Excluded Issuances\"):
>
> \(A\) shares of Common Stock (and options or warrants to purchase such shares) issued or issuable to employees, consultants, officers, or directors of the Corporation pursuant to equity incentive plans or agreements approved by the Board of Directors of the Corporation, including the affirmative vote of the Series A Director, not to exceed in the aggregate such number of shares as are reserved for issuance under the Corporation\'s equity incentive plan as approved by the Board of Directors (and any increases to such plan approved by the Board of Directors, including the Series A Director);
>
> \(B\) shares of Common Stock issuable upon conversion of the Series A Preferred Stock;
>
> \(C\) shares of Common Stock (or options or warrants therefor) issued in connection with bona fide acquisitions, mergers, or similar transactions approved by the Board of Directors, including the affirmative vote of the Series A Director;
>
> \(D\) shares of Common Stock (or warrants therefor) issued to equipment lessors, banks, or other financial institutions in connection with commercial lending, leasing, or similar transactions approved by the Board of Directors, including the affirmative vote of the Series A Director;
>
> \(E\) shares of Common Stock (or options or warrants therefor) issued in connection with sponsored research, collaboration, technology license, development, marketing, or other similar agreements or strategic partnerships approved by the Board of Directors, including the affirmative vote of the Series A Director, provided that the aggregate number of shares issued pursuant to this clause (E) does not exceed one percent (1%) of the Corporation\'s fully diluted capitalization at the time of each such issuance; and
>
> \(F\) shares of Common Stock issued or issuable as a dividend or distribution on the Preferred Stock or pursuant to any event for which adjustment is made pursuant to Section 4.3.5(c)(iv) below.
>
> \(iii\) *Deemed Issuances.* If the Corporation at any time or from time to time after the date of filing of this Certificate shall issue any options, warrants, or other rights to subscribe for or purchase Common Stock (\"Options\") or shall issue any securities convertible into or exchangeable for Common Stock (\"Convertible Securities\"), then the maximum number of shares of Common Stock issuable upon exercise of such Options or upon conve

rsion or exchange of such Convertible Securities shall be deemed to be Additional Shares of Common Stock issued as of the date of issuance of such Options or Convertible Securities, at a price per share equal to the quotient obtained by dividing (x) the aggregate consideration, if any, received by the Corporation for the issuance of such Options or Convertible Securities, plus the minimum aggregate amount of additional consideration payable to the Corporation upon exercise of such Options or upon conversion or exchange of such Convertible Securities, by (y) the maximum number of shares of Common Stock issuable upon exercise of such Options or upon conversion or exchange of such Convertible Securities.
>
> \(iv\) *Adjustments for Stock Splits, Combinations, Dividends, and Distributions.* If the Corporation shall at any time or from time to time after the date of filing of this Certificate (A) pay a dividend or make a distribution on its Common Stock in shares of Common Stock, (B) subdivide its outstanding shares of Common Stock into a greater number of shares, or (C) combine its outstanding shares of Common Stock into a smaller number of shares, then the Conversion Price in effect immediately prior to such action shall be proportionately adjusted so that the number of shares of Common Stock issuable upon conversion of each share of Series A Preferred Stock shall be proportionately increased or decreased, as applicable.

**Section 4.3.6 Voting Rights.** (a) **General Voting Rights**. Each holder of outstanding shares of Series A Preferred Stock shall be entitled to cast the number of votes equal to the number of whole shares of Common Stock into which the shares of Series A Preferred Stock held by such holder are convertible as of the record date for determining stockholders entitled to vote on such matter. Except as otherwise required by applicable law or as expressly provided in this Certificate (including, without limitation, Section 4.3.8), the holders of Series A Preferred Stock shall vote together with the holders of Common Stock as a single class on all matters submitted to a vote of the stockholders.

\(b\) **Election of Directors**. The holders of record of the shares of Series A Preferred Stock, exclusively and as a separate class, shall be entitled to elect one (1) member of the Board of Directors (the \"Series A Director\"). The holders of record of the shares of Common Stock, exclusively and as a separate class, shall be entitled to elect two (2) members of the Board of Directors (each, a \"Common Director\"). The holders of record of the shares of Common Stock and the shares of Preferred Stock, voting together as a single class on an as-converted-to-Common-Stock basis, shall be entitled to elect two (2) additional members of the Board of Directors (each, an \"At-Large Director\"). The total number of directors constituting the entire Board of Directors shall be five (5), subject to the provisions of Article V and the Protective Provisions set forth in Section 4.3.8 hereof.

\(c\) **Vacancies**. Any vacancy in the position of any director elected pursuant to Section 4.3.6(b) above shall be filled only by the affirmative vote or written consent of the holders of the class or classes of stock entitled to elect such director, or by the remaining director or directors elected by such class or classes of stock. Any director elected pursuant to Section 4.3.6(b) may be removed during his or her term of office, with or without cause, by and only by the affirmative vote or written consent of the holders of a majority of the shares of the class or classes of stock entitled to elect such director.

**Section 4.3.7 Redemption.** The shares of Series A Preferred Stock shall not be redeemable at the option of any holder thereof or at the option of the Corporation. No holder of Series A Preferred Stock shall have any right to require the Corporation to redeem or repurchase any shares of Series A Preferred Stock.

**Section 4.3.8 Protective Provisions.** At any time when any shares of Series A Preferred Stock are outstanding, the Corporation shall not, and shall not permit any subsidiary of the Corporation to, directly or indirectly, without the prior written consent or affirmative vote of the holders of at least a majority of the outstanding shares of Preferred Stock (voting as a single class on an as-converted basis), take any of the following actions:

> \(i\) Amend, alter, or repeal any provision of the Certificate of Incorporation or the Bylaws of the Corporation in a manner that adversely affects or changes the rights, preferences, privileges, or powers of the Preferred Stock, including any amendment that alters or changes the powers, preferences, or special rights of the shares of Series A Preferred Stock so as to affect them adversely;
>
> \(ii\) Authorize, create, or issue (by reclassification, merger, or otherwise) any new class or series of capital stock, or any bonds, debentures, notes, or other obligations convertible into or exchangeable for, or having option rights to purchase, any shares of capital stock of the Corporation, having rights, preferences, or privileges senior to or on parity with the Series A Preferred Stock with respect to dividends, liquidation preferences, redemption, voting, or any other rights, or increase the authorized number of shares of any existing series of Preferred Stock;
>
> \(iii\) Increase or decrease (other than by conversion of the Preferred Stock) the total number of authorized shares of Common Stock or Preferred Stock of the Corporation;
>
> \(iv\) Authorize, declare, or pay any dividend on, or make any distribution with respect to, any shares of capital stock of the Corporation, or set aside any funds for any such purpose;
>
> \(v\) Approve, authorize, or consummate any merger, consolidation, sale of all or substantially all of the assets of the Corporation or any subsidiary, or any other Deemed Liquidation Event (as defined in Section 4.3.4), or voluntarily liquidate, dissolve, or wind up the affairs of the Corporation;
>
> \(vi\) Redeem, repurchase, or otherwise acquire (or pay into or set aside for a sinking fund for such purpose) any shares of capital stock of the Corporation, other than the repurchase of shares of Common Stock held by employees, officers, directors, consultants, or other persons performing services for the Corporation or any subsidiary pursuant to agreements under which the Corporation has the right to repurchase such shares at cost or at the lower of cost or fair market value upon the termination of services, in each case as approved by the Board of Directors, including the affirmative vote of the Series A Director;
>
> \(vii\) Increase or decrease the authorized size of the Board of Directors of the Corporation beyond five (5) members;
>
> \(viii\) Create, incur, assume, or suffer to exist any indebtedness (including any guarantee of indebtedness) in excess of Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$500,000) in the aggregate, other than (A) trade payables incurred in the ordinary course of business, (B) equipment financing or leasing transactions in the ordinary course of business approved by the Board of Directors, and (C) indebtedness existing as of the date hereof; or
>
> \(ix\) Enter into any transaction or agreement with any officer, director, employee, or holder of more than one percent (1%) of the Corporation\'s outstanding capital stock, or any member of the immediate family of any such person, or any entity in which any such person is an officer, director, partner, or holder of more than five percent (5%) of such entity\'s outstanding equity, except for (A) customary employment and consulting arrangements and benefit programs on reasonable terms, (B) transactions on terms no less favorable to the Corporation than would be available from unrelated third parties, and (C) transactions approved by a majority of the disinterested members of the Board of Directors.

For the avoidance of doubt, the protective provisions set forth in this Section 4.3.8 shall apply to any action described above whether taken by the Corporation directly or indirectly through any subsidiary, and whether effected by amendment, merger, consolidation, or otherwise. The rights set forth in this Section 4.3.8 shall be in addition to, and not in limitation of, any other voting rights to which the holders of Preferred Stock are entitled under this Certificate, the Bylaws of the Corporation, or applicable law.

**Section 4.3.9 No Reissuance of Preferred Stock.** No share of Series A Preferred Stock acquired by the Corporation by reason of conversion, redemption, repurchase, or otherwise shall be reissued, and all such shares shall be cancelled, retired, and eliminated from the shares that the Corporation is authorized to issue.

**[ARTICLE V]{.underline}**

**[BOARD OF DIRECTORS]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1 Number and Election.**

The number of directors constituting the entire Board of Directors of the Corporation shall be five (5), unless changed as expressly provided in this Certificate of Incorporation or in the Bylaws of the Corporation (subject in all cases to the protective provisions set forth in Section 4.3.8 hereof, which require the consent of the holders of a majority of the outstanding Preferred Stock to increase or decrease the size of the Board of Directors beyond five (5) members). The directors shall be elected as follows:

> \(a\) One (1) director shall be elected by the holders of a majority of the outstanding shares of Series A Preferred Stock, voting exclusively and as a separate class (the \"Series A Director\");
>
> \(b\) Two (2) directors shall be elected by the holders of a majority of the outstanding shares of Common Stock, voting exclusively and as a separate class (each, a \"Common Director\"); and
>
> \(c\) Two (2) directors shall be elected by the holders of a majority of the outstanding shares of Common Stock and Preferred Stock, voting together as a single class on an as-converted-to-Common-Stock basis (each, an \"At-Large Director\").

Unless and until the election of the members of the initial Board of Directors following the filing of this Certificate, the members of the Board of Directors shall be those individuals identified in the records of the Corporation.

**Section 5.2 Removal.**

Any director may be removed from office during such director\'s term, with or without cause, but only by the affirmative vote or written consent of the holders of a majority of the shares of the class or classes of capital stock entitled to elect such director pursuant to Section 5.1 above.

**Section 5.3 Powers.**

The business and affairs of the Corporation shall be managed by or under the direction of the Board of Directors. In addition to the powers and authority expressly conferred upon the Board of Directors by statute, by this Certificate, or by the Bylaws, the Board of Directors is hereby empowered to exercise all such powers and do all such acts and things as may be exercised or done by the Corporation, subject to the provisions of the DGCL, this Certificate, and the Bylaws. All corporate powers of the Corporation shall be vested in and exercised by or under the authority of the Board of Directors, except as otherwise provided by the DGCL, this Certificate, or the Bylaws.

**Section 5.4 Written Ballot Not Required.**

Elections of directors at any meeting of the stockholders need not be by written ballot unless the Bylaws of the Corporation shall otherwise provide. The Board of Directors may fix the number of nominees in advance of any meeting of stockholders, and the Bylaws may provide for procedures governing the nomination of candidates for election as directors.

**[ARTICLE VI]{.underline}**

**[BYLAWS]{.underline}**

In furtherance of, and not in limitation of, the powers conferred by statute, the Board of Directors of the Corporation is expressly authorized to adopt, amend, alter, or repeal the Bylaws of the Corporation. In addition to any vote of the Board of Directors required by law, the Certificate of Incorporation, or the Bylaws, the stockholders of the Corporation shall also have the power to adopt, amend, alter, or repeal the Bylaws of the Corporation; *provided, however*, that any amendment to the Bylaws that would adversely affect the rights, preferences, or privileges of the Preferred Stock shall require the prior approval of the holders of the Preferred Stock as set forth in the Protective Provisions of Section 4.3.8 hereof.

**[ARTICLE VII]{.underline}**

**[LIMITATION OF DIRECTOR LIABILITY]{.underline}**

To the fullest extent permitted by the DGCL, as it presently exists or may hereafter be amended from time to time, no director of the Corporation shall be personally liable to the Corporation or to any of its stockholders for monetary damages for breach of fiduciary duty as a director. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, as permitted by Section 102(b)(7) of the DGCL, the personal liability of a director to the Corporation or its stockholders for monetary damages for breach of fiduciary duty as a director is hereby eliminated; *provided, however*, that this provision shall not eliminate or limit the liability of a director to the extent that such elimination or limitation of liability is not permitted under the DGCL. Without limiting the foregoing, this Article VII shall not eliminate or limit the liability of a director: (a) for any breach of the director\'s duty of loyalty to the Corporation or its stockholders; (b) for acts or omissions not in good faith or which involve intentional misconduct or a knowing violation of law; (c) under Section 174 of the DGCL (relating to unlawful payment of dividends, unlawful stock purchases, and unlawful redemptions); or (d) for any transaction from which the director derived an improper personal benefit.

If the DGCL is amended after the filing of this Certificate to authorize corporate action further eliminating or limiting the personal liability of directors, then the liability of a director of the Corporation shall be eliminated or limited to the fullest extent permitted by the DGCL as so amended, automatically and without further action by the stockholders or directors of the Corporation. Any amendment, repeal, or modification of this Article VII, or the adoption of any provision of this Certificate inconsistent with this Article VII, shall not adversely affect any right or protection of a director of the Corporation existing at the time of such amendment, repeal, modification, or adoption with respect to acts or omissions occurring prior to such amendment, repeal, modification, or adoption.

**[ARTICLE VIII]{.underline}**

**[INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 Right to Indemnification.**

The Corporation shall indemnify, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law as it presently exists or may hereafter be amended, any person who was or is made, or is threatened to be made, a party or is otherwise involved in any threatened, pending, or completed action, suit, or proceeding, whether civil, criminal, administrative, or investigative (a \"Proceeding\"), by reason of the fact that such person, or a person for whom such person is the legal representative, is or was a director or officer of the Corporation or, while serving as a director or officer of the Corporation, is or was serving at the request of the Corporation as a director, officer, employee, or agent of another corporation, partnership, joint venture, trust, enterprise, or nonprofit entity, including service with respect to employee benefit plans maintained or sponsored by the Corporation (an \"Indemnitee\"), against all liability and loss suffered and expenses (including attorneys\' fees, judgments, fines, ERISA excise taxes or penalties, amounts paid or to be paid in settlement, and any other costs and disbursements) reasonably incurred by such Indemnitee in connection therewith. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Corporation shall be required to indemnify an Indemnitee in connection with a Proceeding (or part thereof) commenced by such Indemnitee only if the commencement of such Proceeding (or part thereof) by the Indemnitee was authorized by the Board of Directors.

**Section 8.2 Advancement of Expenses.**

The Corporation shall, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, pay the expenses (including attorneys\' fees) incurred by an Indemnitee in defending any Proceeding in advance of its final disposition; *provided, however*, that, to the extent required by law, such payment of expenses in advance of the final disposition of the Proceeding shall be made only upon receipt of an undertaking by or on behalf of the Indemnitee to repay all amounts so advanced if it shall ultimately be determined by final judicial decision from which there is no further right to appeal that such Indemnitee is not entitled to be indemnified for such expenses under this Article VIII or otherwise.

**Section 8.3 Non-Exclusivity of Rights.**

The rights conferred on any Indemnitee by this Article VIII shall not be exclusive of any other rights that any Indemnitee may have or hereafter acquire under any statute, provision of this Certificate of Incorporation, provision of the Bylaws, agreement, vote of stockholders or disinterested directors, or otherwise. The Corporation is authorized to enter into individual contracts with any or all of its directors, officers, employees, or agents respecting indemnification and advancement of expenses, to the fullest extent not prohibited by the DGCL or other applicable law.

**Section 8.4 Insurance.**

The Corporation may purchase and maintain insurance, at its expense, on behalf of any person who is or was a director, officer, employee, or agent of the Corporation, or is or was serving at the request of the Corporation as a director, officer, employee, or agent of another corporation, partnership, joint venture, trust, enterprise, or nonprofit entity, against any liability asserted against such person and incurred by such person in any such capacity, or arising out of such person\'s status as such, whether or not the Corporation would have the power to indemnify such person against such liability under the provisions of the DGCL.

**[ARTICLE IX]{.underline}**

**[DGCL SECTION 203 OPT-OUT]{.underline}**

The Corporation hereby expressly elects not to be governed by Section 203 of the DGCL. For the avoidance of doubt, the restrictions on business combinations with interested stockholders set forth in Section 203 of the DGCL shall not apply to the Corporation or any of its stockholders, and neither the Corporation nor any of its stockholders shall have any rights or obligations under Section 203 of the DGCL.

**[ARTICLE X]{.underline}**

**[FORUM SELECTION]{.underline}**

Unless the Corporation consents in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, the following provisions shall apply:

> \(a\) The Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware (or, if the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware does not have subject matter jurisdiction, another state court located within the State of Delaware, or if no state court located within the State of Delaware has subject matter jurisdiction, the federal district court for the District of Delaware) shall, to the fullest extent permitted by law, be the sole and exclusive forum for (i) any derivative action or proceeding brought on behalf of the Corporation, (ii) any action asserting a claim of breach of a fiduciary duty owed by any current or former director, officer, employee, agent, or stockholder of the Corporation to the Corporation or to the Corporation\'s stockholders, (iii) any action asserting a claim arising pursuant to any provision of the DGCL, this Certificate of Incorporation, or the Bylaws of the Corporation (as each may be amended or restated from time to time), or (iv) any action asserting a claim governed by the internal affairs doctrine of the State of Delaware.
>
> \(b\) Unless the Corporation consents in writing to the selection of an alternative forum, the federal district courts of the United States of America shall, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, be the sole and exclusive forum for the resolution of any complaint asserting a cause of action arising under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. For the avoidance of doubt, this Section (b) is intended to benefit and may be enforced by the Corporation, its officers and directors, the underwriters to any offering giving rise to such complaint, and any other professional or entity whose consent is required to qualify any such offering.

Any person or entity purchasing or otherwise acquiring or holding any interest in any shares of capital stock of the Corporation shall be deemed to have notice of and to have consented to the provisions of this Article X.

**[ARTICLE XI]{.underline}**

**[AMENDMENT]{.underline}**

The Corporation reserves the right to amend, alter, change, or repeal any provision contained in this Certificate of Incorporation, in the manner now or hereafter prescribed by statute, and all rights and powers conferred upon stockholders, directors, and officers herein are granted subject to this reservation. Any amendment, alteration, change, or repeal of any provision of this Certificate of Incorporation that would adversely affect the rights, preferences, or privileges of the Series A Preferred Stock, or that would amend this Article XI, shall require the prior written consent or affirmative vote of the holders of at least a majority of the outstanding shares of Preferred Stock, voting as a single class, in addition to any other vote required by the DGCL.

**[ARTICLE XII]{.underline}**

**[MISCELLANEOUS]{.underline}**

**Section 12.1 Severability.**

If any provision of this Certificate of Incorporation shall be held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable as applied to any circumstance for any reason whatsoever, the validity, legality, and enforceability of such provision in any other circumstance, and of the remaining provisions of this Certificate (including, without limitation, each portion of any paragraph of this Certificate containing any such provision held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable that is not itself held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable), shall not in any way be affected or impaired thereby.

**Section 12.2 Fiscal Year.**

The fiscal year of the Corporation shall end on December 31 of each year, unless otherwise determined by the Board of Directors.

# ---------------- CRITICAL ----------------
I(id="C-1", pr="Critical", title="Founder non-competition and non-solicitation covenants",
  sec="§7.4(a)-(c); see also §§8.1, 8.2 (survival), 9.4-9.5 (Delaware law and forum), 9.12 (specific performance)",
  src="Term Sheet §5.3; Series A IRA (Key Holder signature page); Massachusetts law; market",
  problem=[
   "Section 7.4 imposes on each Founder a worldwide non-compete covering \"any field related to synthetic biology, industrial biotechnology, or engineered biological systems,\" including any entity \"planning to engage\" in such a field, for the entire period of service plus twenty-four (24) months after separation for any reason, together with a 24-month employee and customer/collaborator non-solicit. Section 7.4(c) asks a court to reform the covenant, and Sections 8.1 and 8.2 make Section 7.4 survive termination of the Agreement, including after an IPO.",
   "This is a direct departure from the executed Term Sheet. Term Sheet §5.3 states that \"[n]o non-competition or non-solicitation provisions are included in this Term Sheet\" and that any employment-related restrictive covenants \"shall be addressed separately in individual employment agreements ... and shall not be a condition of, or otherwise incorporated into, the Series B Financing or any transaction document.\" The Series A IRA went further: its Key Holder signature page expressly states that \"the Key Holders are not subject to any restrictive covenants, non-competition obligations, or non-solicitation obligations under this Agreement.\" The only founder-related covenant the Term Sheet contemplates is continued compliance with the existing CIIAs (§5.3, second paragraph), which is already covered by draft §6.4."],
  risk=[
   "Founder exposure. As drafted, the covenant would bar Priya and Marcus from essentially any work in their scientific field anywhere in the world for two years after any departure, including a termination without cause, and would survive an IPO or sale. Because it sits in an investor agreement rather than an employment agreement, each Investor (not just the Company) could claim standing to enforce it, and §9.12 pre-concedes irreparable harm for injunctive relief.",
   "Massachusetts law. Both Founders live and work in Massachusetts. The Massachusetts Noncompetition Agreement Act (M.G.L. c. 149, §24L) applies to non-competes with employees and independent contractors. It requires, among other things: a signed writing that tells the employee they may consult counsel; at least ten business days' advance notice and \"fair and reasonable consideration\" beyond continued employment for a covenant entered into after employment begins; a restricted period of no more than 12 months (extendable to two years only for breach of fiduciary duty or unlawful taking of company property); garden-leave pay of at least 50% of the employee's highest annualized base salary or other mutually agreed consideration; and geographic and activity scope that is reasonable (presumptively limited to the areas and services of the employee's last two years). The covenant is unenforceable against an employee who is terminated without cause or laid off. Section 24L(e) also bars avoiding Massachusetts law through a choice-of-law clause for an employee who has lived or worked in Massachusetts for at least 30 days before termination, and requires suit in the county where the employee lives or, if the parties agree, Suffolk County. Section 7.4 fails nearly every one of these requirements, and §§9.4-9.5 (Delaware law, exclusive Chancery forum) conflict with §24L(e).",
   "Investors may argue that the Act does not apply because the covenant was \"made outside of an employment relationship\" (a stockholder covenant) or under the sale-of-business exclusion. Neither argument fits a financing in which the Founders sell nothing and the restricted period runs from the end of employment. Even if the argument worked, the covenant would still face common-law reasonableness review. The Delaware Court of Chancery has also recently refused to blue-pencil overbroad covenants and has struck them entirely (e.g., Kodiak Building Partners, LLC v. Adams (Del. Ch. 2022); Sunder Energy, LLC v. Jackson (Del. 2024)). The likely result is an unenforceable but litigable covenant that chills the Founders and gives investors leverage in any separation dispute.",
   "The FTC's 2024 non-compete rule is not a defense: it was set aside nationwide in Ryan LLC v. FTC (N.D. Tex. Aug. 20, 2024) and, in any case, contained a senior-executive carve-out for existing agreements.",
   "Deal risk. The Founders have flagged this as a priority concern, and it was never discussed during term sheet negotiations. Accepting it would re-trade a point the Term Sheet expressly resolved."],
  rec=[
   "Delete §7.4 in its entirety, strike \"7.4\" from §§8.1 and 8.2, and make the Key Holders sign in a limited capacity, as they did in the Series A IRA. Cite Term Sheet §5.3 in the comments letter; this point should not be negotiable. If CMV wants protection, the answer is the existing CIIAs (a closing condition under Term Sheet §5.3) and any separately negotiated, §24L-compliant employment agreements, outside the financing documents.",
   "Proposed replacement language (new §7.4): \"No Restrictive Covenants. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, no Key Holder shall be subject to any non-competition, non-solicitation, no-hire, or similar restrictive covenant under this Agreement. Any such covenant, if applicable, shall be set forth exclusively in a separate written agreement between the Company and such Key Holder, shall be governed by applicable law (including M.G.L. c. 149, §24L), and shall not be a condition to, or otherwise incorporated into, the transactions contemplated by the Purchase Agreement.\""])

I(id="C-2", pr="Critical", title="Differential 270-day Founder lock-up",
  sec="§6.2 (and duplicative §§2.11, 6.1)",
  src="Term Sheet §5.2; Series A IRA §6.1; market (NVCA)",
  problem=[
   "Section 6.2 subjects the Founders alone to a 270-day lock-up that runs from the date of the final prospectus. It covers after-acquired shares, including shares bought in the IPO or in the open market and shares acquired on option exercise, and it bans hedging. Every other Holder gets 180 days under §2.11.",
   "Term Sheet §5.2 is explicit: the lock-up is 180 days, \"uniform for all stockholders and optionholders, with no differential lock-up period applicable to the Founders or any other subset of stockholders,\" and it begins on \"the effective date of the registration statement.\" The Series A IRA §6.1 likewise required a uniform 180-day period \"without differentiation.\" The draft now has three overlapping lock-up provisions (§§2.11, 6.1 and 6.2) with different start dates (effective date versus final prospectus date) and different scope."],
  risk=[
   "Ninety extra days of illiquidity for the Founders alone, beyond whatever the underwriters actually require. The longer period also tells the market that management has been singled out. If the underwriters ask for less, §6.2 still binds the Founders unless the managing underwriter consents. Covering after-acquired shares goes beyond NVCA practice, which covers only shares held immediately before the IPO. Having three overlapping provisions invites disputes over which one governs."],
  rec=[
   "Delete §§6.1 and 6.2 and keep a single NVCA-form market stand-off in §2.11, revised as described in Issue S-4 (uniform 180 days from the effective date, applying only to shares held immediately before the IPO, and binding the Holders only if all officers, directors and 1% holders are similarly bound, with pro rata early-release protection)."])

I(id="C-3", pr="Critical", title="Drag-along triggered by Preferred alone (Common approval and Board approval omitted)",
  sec="§§5.1-5.3",
  src="Term Sheet §5.1; Restated Certificate §§4.3.4(c), 4.3.8(v); Series A IRA (no drag-along); market (NVCA Voting Agreement §3)",
  problem=[
   "Under §5.1, the \"Electing Holders,\" meaning holders of a majority of the outstanding Preferred Stock voting together, can force every Stockholder (including the Founders) to vote for, consent to and support a Sale of the Company. No approval from the Common Stock or the Board is required.",
   "Term Sheet §5.1 defines the \"Requisite Approval\" as a majority of the Preferred Stock (voting together) and a majority of the outstanding Common Stock. Northstar's counsel has also stressed that both had to approve. The Term Sheet also places the drag-along in the Voting Agreement, not the IRA. The Series A IRA had no drag-along at all, so this is a new obligation for the Series A holders and the Founders."],
  risk=[
   "Cap table math (assuming 1:1 conversion and the Term Sheet capitalization): 9,000,000 Preferred shares will be outstanding after the initial Closing (6,000,000 Series A and 3,000,000 Series B), so a majority requires more than 4,500,000. CMV (2,117,647) plus Verdant (2,400,000) holds 4,517,647 shares. Those two holders alone could therefore drag Northstar, Pinnacle and both Founders into a sale. The Series A holders voting alone (6,000,000) could also drag the Series B. The Founders hold 4,200,000 Common shares, roughly 32% of the as-converted equity, and would have no say at all. This is exactly the \"squeeze-out\" scenario Northstar raised.",
   "There is no requirement that the Board approve the transaction. A merger requires Board approval under DGCL §251 in any event, and a drag without Board approval invites fiduciary-duty disputes. The draft also does not address the Series A majority's separate-class right under Restated Certificate §4.3.4(a) to elect not to treat a transaction as a Deemed Liquidation Event. That right must be reconciled in the Series B charter.",
   "The protective conditions in §5.2 are helpful and should be kept: same per-share consideration within a class, liability several and capped at proceeds, limited reps, and no forced non-compete or non-solicit. Note that §5.2(d) appropriately refuses to force non-competes in a sale, which cannot be squared with §7.4."],
  rec=[
   "Move the drag-along to the Voting Agreement as the Term Sheet requires (or, if it stays here, conform it exactly to the Voting Agreement) and revise the trigger to require the Term Sheet's Requisite Approval plus Board approval.",
   "Proposed language for §5.1 lead-in: \"In the event that each of (i) the Board, (ii) the holders of at least a majority of the outstanding shares of Preferred Stock, voting together as a single class on an as-converted basis, and (iii) the holders of at least a majority of the then-outstanding shares of Common Stock (other than shares of Common Stock issued or issuable upon conversion of Preferred Stock) (the approvals in clauses (ii) and (iii), together, the \"Requisite Approval\") approve a Sale of the Company in writing, then ...\".",
   "Add to §5.2 an express condition that the proceeds be allocated per the liquidation provisions of the Restated Certificate as in effect immediately before the sale (Term Sheet §5.1). Add that each holder of a class gets the same form-of-consideration election, and that any indemnity is several and not joint (consistent with the Term Sheet's \"customary limitations\")."])

I(id="C-4", pr="Critical", title="Board composition provisions contradict the Term Sheet and the Certificate",
  sec="§6.7",
  src="Term Sheet §4.1; Restated Certificate §§4.3.6(b), 4.3.8(vii), 5.1; Series A IRA §5.4",
  problem=[
   "Section 6.7 fixes the Board at five seats: (a) one Series A designee; (b) one designee of a majority of the Series B; (c) one designee of a majority of the Common; (d) the CEO (initially Priya); and (e) one independent director \"mutually acceptable to the other directors then serving.\" It also locks the Board at five directors \"[f]or so long as this Agreement remains in effect.\"",
   "Term Sheet §4.1 provides for: two Common seats (initially Priya and Marcus); one Series A seat; one seat designated by CMV (initially Joanna Xu), not by a majority of the Series B; and one independent director mutually agreed by a majority of the Common and a majority of the Preferred. It places Board composition in the Voting Agreement. The current Restated Certificate (§§4.3.6(b), 5.1) provides for two Common Directors, one Series A Director and two At-Large Directors, and changing Board size requires Preferred consent (§4.3.8(vii))."],
  risk=[
   "The Founders lose a guaranteed seat. Marcus has no seat at all, and the Common's second seat becomes a CEO seat that follows the office. If the Board replaces Priya as CEO, the Founders' representation falls to one seat. The independent director is chosen by the other directors, not by the Common and Preferred jointly, which hands effective control of that seat, and so of the Board (3 of 5), to the investor designees. Designating the Series B seat by \"majority of Series B\" rather than CMV also departs from the Term Sheet. It would let CMV and Pinnacle jointly control the seat; Pinnacle cannot control it alone because CMV holds about 71% of the Series B.",
   "Structurally, a board-election covenant in an IRA that has no voting-agreement or proxy machinery (DGCL §218(c)) is unclear and may conflict with the charter's class-election provisions. Locking Board size at five in the IRA also overrides the charter, under which size can change with Preferred consent. The Company would need an IRA amendment as well as charter compliance."],
  rec=[
   "Delete the composition sentences of §6.7 and implement Term Sheet §4.1 in the Voting Agreement and the Series B Restated Certificate (two Common Directors, one Series A Director, one CMV designee, and one independent director approved by a majority of the Common and a majority of the Preferred). Keep the last sentence of §6.7 (quarterly meetings and expense reimbursement), which tracks Series A IRA §5.4. Delete the size lock-in, which is already covered by the charter protective provision."])

I(id="C-5", pr="Critical", title="Termination provision: wrong triggers, wrong threshold, survival of non-compete, and an internal defect that wipes out registration rights at the IPO",
  sec="§§8.1, 8.2 (and §§2.1(a), 2.4, 2.9, 2.11, 3.4, 4.6)",
  src="Term Sheet §5.4; Series A IRA §§2.10, 7.11; internal consistency; market (NVCA §§2.13, 6.6)",
  problem=[
   "Triggers. Term Sheet §5.4 (and Series A IRA §7.11) terminate the IRA on the earliest of (a) a Qualified IPO, (b) a Deemed Liquidation Event, or (c) the written consent of the Company and a majority of the Registrable Securities. Draft §8.1 deletes the Deemed Liquidation Event trigger and raises the consent threshold to two-thirds of the Registrable Securities.",
   "Survival. Section 8.1 carves out §7.4 (the non-compete) so that it survives every termination event. Section 8.2 refers to \"this Section 9\" even though it sits in Section 8 (a drafting error). The survival list also omits the confidentiality covenant (§3.2(b)), which survived termination under Series A IRA §7.11.",
   "Internal defect. Because the entire Agreement terminates \"upon ... the closing of the Company's initial public offering,\" every right that only matters after the IPO dies the moment it becomes usable: the demand right exercisable 180 days after the IPO (§2.1(a)(ii)), Form S-3 rights available only \"[a]fter the closing of the Company's IPO\" (§2.4), Rule 144 reporting (§2.9) and the market stand-off itself (§§2.11, 6.1, 6.2). The draft also contains no registration-rights sunset of the kind found in Series A IRA §2.10 or NVCA §2.13. The Term Sheet language (\"the IRA shall terminate automatically upon ... a Qualified IPO\") has the same flaw; NVCA practice terminates the covenants and ROFO at the IPO but keeps registration rights, subject to their own sunset."],
  risk=[
   "Lock-in. Without a Deemed Liquidation Event trigger, the investor covenants (including the observer, information and pay-to-play provisions) could survive into an acquirer's ownership, complicating any sale. A two-thirds consent threshold gives small coalitions a blocking position. For example, Northstar plus Pinnacle (about 4.48M shares), or CMV plus the Founders, can block if the Founders' Common counts as Registrable Securities (about 13.2M in total). Because §9.2 permits amendment by a simple majority, the two-thirds threshold is also internally incoherent: a majority could simply amend §8.1. Diana asked us to confirm the Company is not locked in longer than agreed, and on these points it would be.",
   "The registration-rights defect will be found and fixed by CMV's counsel eventually. It is better for the Company to propose a company-favorable fix now than to accept whatever comes back later. The non-compete survival compounds Issue C-1.",
   "IPO versus Qualified IPO. The Term Sheet uses a Qualified IPO ($50M gross proceeds at no less than 3x the Series B Original Issue Price, i.e., $25.50 per share). The draft uses any IPO, and its \"IPO\" definition has no size threshold (the Series A IRA required $30M). Terminating on any IPO is actually better for the Company, because under the Term Sheet a smaller IPO would leave private-company information and ROFO rights alive in a public company. We recommend keeping \"IPO\" for Sections 3, 4 and 6 and explaining the rationale; consistent with Term Sheet §3.2, add Exchange Act reporting status as an alternative trigger."],
  rec=[
   "Proposed §8.1: \"This Agreement shall terminate and be of no further force or effect upon the earliest to occur of (a) the closing of the IPO, (b) the consummation of a Deemed Liquidation Event, and (c) the written consent of the Company and the holders of at least a majority of the Registrable Securities then outstanding; provided, however, that (i) upon an event described in clause (a), Section 2 shall survive and shall terminate in accordance with Section 2.13, and (ii) Sections 2.7, 2.8, 3.2(b) (for a period of [two (2)] years following termination), 8 and 9 shall survive any termination.\"",
   "Add a new §2.13 (Termination of Registration Rights) along the lines of Series A IRA §2.10 and NVCA §2.13: registration rights terminate at the earliest of (i) a Deemed Liquidation Event, (ii) as to any Holder, when all of its Registrable Securities can be sold under Rule 144 in a 90-day period without volume or manner-of-sale limits, and (iii) the [third] anniversary of the IPO.",
   "Correct the cross-reference in §8.2, delete \"7.4\" from §§8.1 and 8.2, and conform §§3.4 and 4.6 to the revised §8.1."])

I(id="C-6", pr="Critical", title="Major Investor threshold doubled to 1,000,000 shares; second-tier information rights",
  sec="§§1.12, 3.5 (also §§2.4, 3.1-3.3, 4.1, 9.9)",
  src="Term Sheet §§3.1 (S-3), 3.2, 3.3, 3.4; Series A IRA §1.15",
  problem=[
   "The draft defines \"Major Investor\" as a holder of at least 1,000,000 shares of Preferred Stock. The Term Sheet sets the threshold at 500,000 shares, both for information rights (§3.2) and for the ROFO (§3.3). The S-3 and inspection rights (§§3.1, 3.4) also run to \"Major Investors\" as defined in the Term Sheet. The Series A IRA used 500,000 shares.",
   "Section 3.5 then creates a second tier: holders of at least 500,000 but fewer than 1,000,000 shares receive only the annual and quarterly financial statements. They get no budget, no capitalization table, no inspection and no ROFO. Under the Term Sheet, 500,000-share holders were entitled to all four §3.2 deliverables."],
  risk=[
   "Pinnacle (882,353 Series B shares, $7.5M and about 25% of the round) falls below the threshold. It would lose its pro rata right, its S-3 initiation right, inspection and most information rights. Any additional investor in the up-to-$4.5M subsequent closing (at most about 529,411 shares at $8.50) would also be excluded. Northstar (3.6M) and Verdant (2.4M) qualify today, but the higher bar narrows their cushion against any partial transfer or fund restructuring. That is precisely the \"definition thresholds\" concern Northstar's counsel raised.",
   "For the Company, a higher threshold does reduce the number of recipients. But it is a Term Sheet re-trade that Pinnacle and Northstar will reject, and it risks delaying the March 5 signing. It also invites a demand for a more investor-favorable concession elsewhere."],
  rec=[
   "Restore the 500,000-share threshold in §1.12 (as adjusted for splits and similar events, with affiliate aggregation) and delete the proviso in §3.5. Consider adding the NVCA exclusion of any investor the Board reasonably determines to be a competitor of the Company (see Issue S-5)."])

I(id="C-7", pr="Critical", title="New contractual pay-to-play strips ROFO and information rights",
  sec="§4.5",
  src="Term Sheet (silent; not agreed); Series A IRA (none); Restated Certificate (none)",
  problem=[
   "Under §4.5, any Major Investor that fails to buy its full Pro Rata Share in any \"Qualified Financing\" (any Preferred financing of $5M or more) automatically loses both its ROFO and all of its Section 3 information rights. The suspension continues until it buys its full Pro Rata Share in a later Qualified Financing. Nothing like this appears in the Term Sheet or the Series A IRA."],
  risk=[
   "This hits existing investors hardest: a seed-stage fund such as Northstar, or an angel vehicle such as Verdant, may not have reserves to take a full pro rata share in every round. A deep-pocketed lead like CMV benefits disproportionately. Northstar has specifically warned it does not want to be \"squeezed out,\" and losing information rights for not participating is the clearest version of that.",
   "Drafting gaps: the provision does not say how \"full Pro Rata Share\" works if the Company or a new lead caps the insiders' allocation. It does not explain how a suspended investor can ever re-qualify if it is no longer receiving information. It also does not align with the 15-day ROFO window. Because the Prior Agreement can only be amended with the consent of a majority of the Registrable Securities (Series A IRA §7.6), Northstar (60% of the Series A) effectively controls whether the amendment and restatement happens. Insisting on §4.5 risks Northstar refusing to sign."],
  rec=[
   "Delete §4.5. If a pay-to-play is to be considered in a future down-round, it belongs in the charter and should be approved at that time by the Board and the requisite stockholders."])

I(id="C-8", pr="Critical", title="Unlimited audit rights at the Company's expense",
  sec="§3.3",
  src="Term Sheet §3.4; Series A IRA §3.2; market (NVCA has no audit right)",
  problem=[
   "Section 3.3 gives each Major Investor the right, at the Company's expense, to audit the Company's books and records \"at any time\" on five business days' notice, through an auditor of its choosing, with the Company to \"cooperate fully\" and provide access to personnel and systems. There is no limit on frequency, scope or cost.",
   "Term Sheet §3.4 grants only \"standard inspection rights,\" at the Major Investor's sole expense, during business hours, on at least five business days' notice, subject to confidentiality, and without unreasonable interference with the business. The Series A IRA §3.2 inspection right was at the investor's expense, limited to once per calendar year, and excluded trade secrets."],
  risk=[
   "With 47 employees and a $1.8M monthly burn, repeated third-party audits by several Major Investors (four at a 500,000 threshold) could cost the Company real money and consume significant finance-team time, all duplicating the annual audit by Thornburgh & Associates that §3.1(a) already requires. There is no confidentiality obligation on the investor's auditor. This is precisely the \"unlimited audit rights\" Priya asked us to watch for."],
  rec=[
   "Delete §3.3 and rely on the revised inspection right in §3.2(a) (Issue S-6)."])

I(id="C-9", pr="Critical", title="Litigation, regulatory and IP reporting obligation (privilege and trade-secret risk)",
  sec="§3.1(f)",
  src="Term Sheet §3.2 (four enumerated deliverables only); Series A IRA §3.1; market",
  problem=[
   "Section 3.1(f) requires \"detailed reports\" of all pending and threatened litigation, regulatory proceedings and IP prosecution matters, including copies of all material correspondence with the USPTO, the FDA and other agencies. Reports are due quarterly or \"more frequently upon written request,\" with supporting materials sufficient to apprise investors of \"potential impact.\" None of this is in the Term Sheet, which lists only quarterly financials, annual audited financials, the budget and a capitalization table, or in the Series A IRA. The reference to the FDA does not even fit a company that makes engineered microorganisms for industrial chemical production. It appears to be carried over from a health-care form."],
  risk=[
   "Privilege. Sharing counsel's assessments of threatened claims with investors generally waives the attorney-client privilege and may waive work-product protection; the common-interest doctrine is unreliable for minority investors. Trade secrets. Unpublished patent prosecution correspondence (office actions, claim amendments, responses) is among the Company's most sensitive information. CMV and Pinnacle both run life-sciences portfolios that may include competitors, and §3.2(b) lets investors share information with Affiliates and \"financing sources.\" Burden. Preparing \"detailed\" quarterly reports, on demand, is a meaningful drain on a small legal and IP function."],
  rec=[
   "Delete §3.1(f). If CMV presses, offer at most a high-level quarterly summary of material pending litigation, delivered to the Board (not to every Major Investor), excluding privileged material and unpublished IP filings. Add the NVCA withholding proviso described in Issue S-5."])

I(id="C-10", pr="Critical", title="CMV Board Observer: no confidentiality, privilege or conflict guardrails",
  sec="§6.5",
  src="Term Sheet §4.2; market (NVCA observer language); client concern (e)",
  problem=[
   "Section 6.5 gives CMV's observer the right to attend all regular and special Board meetings and to receive all notices, minutes, written consents and other materials \"at the same time and in the same manner\" as directors. It has no confidentiality undertaking, no right to exclude the observer or withhold materials, no limit to Board (as opposed to committee) matters, no fiduciary-duty disclaimer and no termination. Term Sheet §4.2 expressly contemplated that confidentiality obligations and the \"circumstances under which the Observer may be excluded\" would be addressed in the definitive documents. The draft omits them entirely.",
   "The observer is in addition to CMV's Board seat, so CMV will have two people in the boardroom."],
  risk=[
   "Privilege. A non-director, non-fiduciary observer present for privileged legal advice can destroy the privilege for those discussions. Conflicts. Board sessions on matters in which CMV is adverse to the Company (future financings led by CMV, pay-to-play or ROFO disputes, transactions with CMV portfolio companies) would be fully visible to CMV. Competitive information. CMV is a life-sciences-focused fund with a broad portfolio; without a written confidentiality agreement and a competitor-employee bar, the observer could be someone who also sits on a competitor's board. The observer is also not a party to the IRA, so §3.2(b) does not clearly bind them."],
  rec=[
   "Revise §6.5 to add NVCA-style guardrails. Proposed language: \"... provided, however, that (i) such representative shall agree in writing, as a condition to attending any meeting or receiving any materials, to hold in confidence and trust all information so provided on terms no less protective than Section 3.2(b), and CMV shall be responsible for any breach thereof; (ii) the Company reserves the right to withhold any information and to exclude such representative from any meeting or portion thereof if the Board (or the chair of the meeting) reasonably determines that access to such information or attendance at such meeting could (A) adversely affect the attorney-client privilege or attorney work product protection between the Company and its counsel, (B) result in disclosure of trade secrets or highly confidential proprietary information, (C) involve a matter in which CMV or any of its Affiliates or portfolio companies has an interest that conflicts with the interests of the Company, including any transaction or negotiation with, or dispute involving, CMV or its Affiliates, or (D) result in a conflict of interest or violation of applicable law or of a confidentiality obligation to a third party; (iii) the Board may meet in executive session without the observer; (iv) the observer shall not be an employee, officer, director or consultant of any competitor of the Company; (v) the observer shall have no vote, shall not count toward a quorum, owes no fiduciary duty to the Company, and shall have no right to attend committee meetings; and (vi) the rights in this Section 6.5 are personal to CMV, are not assignable, and terminate upon the earliest of the termination of this Agreement and the date CMV ceases to hold at least [50%] of the shares of Series B Preferred Stock purchased by it under the Purchase Agreement.\""])
